title.suggested: Goss Awarded Fight Over Allen on a Foul in Kentucky

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat reported the Goss-Allen championship fight in Boone County, Kentucky, where referee Eph Holland gave the fight to Goss on a foul in the 21st round, though Allen had the better of the fighting.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Saturday Morning, September 9, 1876. The article itself does not give the fight date; it took place on the Thursday before (September 7, 1876).

facts.fact: Allen fought Joe Goss for the championship of America near Walton, Boone County, Kentucky; in the 21st round Allen struck Goss as he went down and referee Eph Holland gave the fight to Goss on a foul. The whole fight lasted 1 hour 50 minutes
Allen weighed 174 pounds to Goss' 165, was the taller man with the longer reach, and was four years younger than Goss; both were described as bald-headed with gray hair

Kentucky militia under Acting Adjutant General W. G. Lobben stopped the fight in the seventh round (35 minutes); the crowd moved by train about eight miles to the farm of P. Lane, about a mile from Walton in Boone County, where the fight resumed at 11 a.m.
places: farm of P. Lane, near Walton, Boone County, Kentucky

facts.fact: After the decision Red Leary offered to let the fight go on for a fresh $1,000 a side, but Allen declined, saying he could not have fair play
Allen laughed and answered Goss in the ninth round
facts.quote: That will be all right, Joe.

facts.fact: When O'Leary said Allen didn't like the gaff, Allen replied
facts.quote: I'd like to know who does, if he can avoid it.

facts.fact: Allen published a card in the Cincinnati evening papers saying it was impossible to get fair play in this country and announcing his withdrawal from the ring

notes: The current title says the fight ended in a draw, which is wrong: Goss was awarded it on a foul. The current summary's 'alleged foul' is softer than the article, which calls the last blow clearly a foul while saying Allen had the best of the fight.
